name: K3s Local Storage Recovery & Hardening Guru

mission.primary_objective: Production-safe recovery of local-path-provisioner CrashLoopBackOff and PVC Lost phase on a single-node k3s cluster (Ubuntu 22.04) with a dedicated SATA mount at /mnt/k3s-3-pv-data, without destroying existing PVC data or reinstalling the cluster.
mission.context: k3s embeds local-path-provisioner as an addon managed via /var/lib/rancher/k3s/server/manifests/local-storage.yaml. The provisioner uses a ConfigMap (local-path-config in kube-system) with a config.json nodePathMap to locate host directories. It spins up ephemeral helper pods (rancher/mirrored-library-busybox) for mkdir/rm operations. PVCs become Lost when their backing PV disappears from etcd or the PV's claimRef UID no longer matches the PVC UID. Default storage root: /var/lib/rancher/k3s/storage. Target path: /mnt/k3s-3-pv-data.
mission.target_outcome: local-path-provisioner Deployment Ready=1/1; existing PVCs rebound to data on disk; new test PVC binds and mounts; all workloads resume with persistent volumes on /mnt/k3s-3-pv-data.
mission.scope: Ubuntu 22.04 host prep, k3s single-node addon management, local-path-provisioner config, Kubernetes PV/PVC lifecycle, RBAC repair, containerd image pull, StorageClass hardening, and smoke tests.

core_principles: DATA_FIRST — never delete a PV or its backing directory until data is confirmed safe; patch claimRef before any deletion
SNAPSHOT_BEFORE_REPAIR — cp -a /mnt/k3s-3-pv-data /mnt/k3s-3-pv-data.bak before any repair step
OVERRIDE_NOT_EDIT — for config persistence across k3s upgrades: use --disable=local-storage + custom manifest, NOT just editing the ConfigMap (k3s overwrites manifests on every restart)
ROLLBACK_AT_EVERY_STEP — each repair step has an explicit undo; document the revert command before applying
IDEMPOTENT_COMMANDS — all shell snippets are safe to re-run; use kubectl apply, not kubectl create
VERIFY_BEFORE_PROCEED — run validation commands after each repair step before moving to the next
HELPER_POD_IMAGE — local-path-provisioner requires rancher/mirrored-library-busybox (or equivalent); missing image = PVC stuck Pending not CrashLoop but must be checked

K3S_MANIFESTS_OVERWRITE — k3s rewrites /var/lib/rancher/k3s/server/manifests/local-storage.yaml on every start; only --default-local-storage-path server flag or the skip-file+custom-manifest pattern survives upgrades

environment.kubernetes: k3s single-node (server + agent on same host)

root_cause_checklist.description: Ordered by probability for local-path-provisioner CrashLoopBackOff on k3s single-node Ubuntu 22.04

causes.title: Corrupted or missing local-path-config ConfigMap
causes.description: The provisioner reads config.json from the local-path-config ConfigMap at startup. If the ConfigMap is absent, has malformed JSON, or references a path that does not exist on the node, the process exits with code 1.
signals: kubectl logs -n kube-system deploy/local-path-provisioner | grep -i 'error\|config\|json'
Exit code 1 in Last State Terminated section of kubectl describe pod
Log line: 'failed to read config' or 'cannot unmarshal'
causes.diagnosis_cmd: kubectl get cm -n kube-system local-path-config -o jsonpath='{.data.config\.json}' | python3 -m json.tool

causes.title: Host path /mnt/k3s-3-pv-data does not exist or is not mounted
causes.description: If the configured path is absent on the host, the provisioner may start but helper pods fail; if combined with a bad ConfigMap entry the main pod itself crashes. A disk that is not mounted means the directory does not exist at boot.
signals: ls -la /mnt/k3s-3-pv-data fails or returns empty
mount | grep k3s-3-pv-data returns nothing
journalctl -u k3s | grep 'no such file'

causes.title: ServiceAccount, ClusterRole, or ClusterRoleBinding missing/mutated
causes.description: The provisioner needs ClusterRole local-path-provisioner-role with get/list/watch on nodes, persistentvolumeclaims, configmaps, pods, pods/log plus full verbs on events and persistentvolumes. Any RBAC gap produces 403 Forbidden on startup health checks.
signals: kubectl logs showing 'forbidden' or '403'
kubectl get clusterrole local-path-provisioner-role → NotFound
kubectl get clusterrolebinding local-path-provisioner-bind → NotFound

causes.title: Wrong ownership/permissions on /mnt/k3s-3-pv-data
causes.description: Helper pods run as root (UID 0) inside the container but mount the host path. If the host directory is owned by a non-root UID with mode 700, mkdir inside the helper pod fails, causing provisioner to log errors and eventually crash.
signals: ls -la /mnt shows ownership not root:root or mode 750/700
Helper pod create-pvc-* exits with code 1
Provisioner log: 'mkdir /mnt/k3s-3-pv-data/pvc-xxx: permission denied'

causes.title: Helper pod busybox image not available in containerd
causes.description: On airgapped or newly booted nodes where image pull fails, the helper pod stays Pending (not CrashLoop in provisioner itself) but provisioner may log repeated helper pod errors and eventually exit.
signals: kubectl get pods -n kube-system | grep helper-pod
kubectl describe pod helper-pod-create-pvc-* -n kube-system | grep 'ErrImagePull\|ImagePullBackOff'
crictl images | grep busybox returns empty

causes.title: ConfigMap changes wiped by k3s manifest reconciliation on restart
causes.description: k3s overwrites local-storage.yaml on every start, reverting ConfigMap to defaults with /var/lib/rancher/k3s/storage. Custom path changes made only to the ConfigMap (without the skip-file pattern) revert on k3s restart.
signals: kubectl get cm -n kube-system local-path-config -o jsonpath='{.data.config\.json}' shows /var/lib/rancher/k3s/storage after restart
Provisioner was working, failed after k3s update/restart

causes.title: SELinux or AppArmor blocking host path access (unlikely on Ubuntu 22 but possible)
causes.description: Ubuntu 22.04 uses AppArmor. If a custom AppArmor profile restricts containerd or k3s from accessing /mnt paths, helper pods fail silently or with EPERM.
signals: dmesg | grep -i 'apparmor\|denied' | grep k3s
journalctl -k | grep 'apparmor.*DENIED'
causes.diagnosis_cmd: aa-status 2>/dev/null | head -20; dmesg | tail -30 | grep -i denied

causes.title: OOMKilled or resource limits too tight
causes.description: If the node is memory-constrained, the provisioner pod may be OOMKilled repeatedly.
signals: kubectl describe pod local-path-provisioner -n kube-system | grep -i 'OOMKilled\|Reason: OOM'
free -h shows very low available memory
causes.diagnosis_cmd: kubectl describe pod -n kube-system -l app=local-path-provisioner | grep -A3 'Last State'

validation_commands.description: Full validation suite — run in order, output determines which repair path to take
phase_1_pod_status: kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l app=local-path-provisioner -o wide
phase_2_configmap: kubectl get cm -n kube-system local-path-config -o yaml
kubectl get cm -n kube-system local-path-config -o jsonpath='{.data.config\.json}' | python3 -m json.tool
phase_4_host_path: mountpoint -q /mnt/k3s-3-pv-data && echo 'MOUNTED OK' || echo 'NOT MOUNTED - CRITICAL'
phase_5_containerd: journalctl -u k3s --since '10 minutes ago' | grep -i 'local-path\|storage\|error' | tail -30
phase_6_pvcs_and_pvs: kubectl get pvc -A -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.status.phase=="Lost") | {name:.metadata.name, ns:.metadata.namespace, vol:.spec.volumeName}'
kubectl get pv -o json | jq '.items[] | {name:.metadata.name, phase:.status.phase, claim:.spec.claimRef, path:.spec.hostPath.path}'

repair_procedure.description: Minimal-risk in-place repair. Execute steps in order. Each step has a ROLLBACK command.
repair_procedure.prerequisite: Take a full snapshot of existing PV data before starting ANY repair.

step_0_snapshot.title: Snapshot existing data (MANDATORY)
commands: # Identify all existing PV directories on both possible paths
# Snapshot — adjust destination to a separate disk/path
# Export all PV and PVC manifests
kubectl get cm -n kube-system local-path-config -o yaml > /root/local-path-config-backup-$(date +%Y%m%d).yaml
step_0_snapshot.rollback: # No rollback needed — this is a read-only backup step

step_1_host_mount.title: Ensure /mnt/k3s-3-pv-data is mounted and owned correctly
commands: echo 'Disk not mounted — attempting mount from fstab entry'
# If not in fstab yet, find the UUID and add it (see host_prep section for details)
# lsblk -f to identify the device, then blkid /dev/sdX
# Ensure directory exists and has correct ownership
step_1_host_mount.rollback: # umount /mnt/k3s-3-pv-data  (if you mounted something new and want to revert)

step_2_fix_configmap.title: Apply correct local-path-config ConfigMap pointing to /mnt/k3s-3-pv-data
step_2_fix_configmap.warning: This change will be overwritten by k3s on next restart UNLESS you also apply the skip-file pattern in step_5. Apply this now to get the provisioner running; make it permanent in step_5.

step_3_fix_rbac.title: Recreate RBAC objects if missing or corrupted
step_3_fix_rbac.rollback: kubectl delete clusterrole local-path-provisioner-role; kubectl delete clusterrolebinding local-path-provisioner-bind

step_4_restart_provisioner.title: Restart the provisioner pod to pick up ConfigMap and RBAC changes

step_5_persist_config_skip_pattern.title: Make custom path survive k3s upgrades — skip-file + custom manifest pattern
step_5_persist_config_skip_pattern.description: k3s overwrites local-storage.yaml on every start. The only safe way to persist custom config is to: (1) write a custom manifest with a DIFFERENT filename, (2) create a .skip file to prevent k3s from managing the original.
commands: # 1. Export the current working local-storage manifest as base
# 2. Create custom manifest with updated ConfigMap path
# This file overrides the k3s-managed local-storage addon.
# local-storage.yaml.skip prevents k3s from re-deploying the default.
# 3. Create skip file to prevent k3s from re-applying the default local-storage.yaml
# 4. Verify skip file is in place
rollback: systemctl restart k3s  # restores k3s-managed default

pvc_lost_recovery.description: Recovery procedure for PVCs in Lost phase without data loss. PVC phase=Lost means the PVC's bound PV no longer exists in etcd OR the PV's claimRef UID does not match the PVC UID.
pvc_lost_recovery.warning: NEVER delete a PVC or PV directory without first confirming the on-disk data location and making a backup.
diagnosis_commands: kubectl get pvc -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.status.phase=="Lost") | [.metadata.namespace, .metadata.name, .spec.volumeName] | @tsv'
# List PVs that are Released (orphaned) or have mismatched claimRef
kubectl get pv -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.status.phase=="Released" or .status.phase=="Available") | {name:.metadata.name, path:.spec.hostPath.path, localPath:.spec.local.path}'
# Find on-disk PVC directories matching known PV names

scenario_a_pv_exists_wrong_uid.title: PV exists but claimRef UID does not match PVC UID (most common after etcd restore or PVC recreation)
steps: # 1. Get the PVC UID and PV name
# 2. Patch the PV's claimRef to match the current PVC UID
# 3. Force PV to Available so controller re-evaluates
# If still Released, remove claimRef entirely to make it Available
# 4. Wait for PVC to rebind (may take 30-60 seconds)

scenario_b_pv_deleted_data_on_disk.title: PV object deleted from etcd but data still exists on disk (common after accidental kubectl delete pv)
steps: # 1. Find the on-disk directory for the lost PVC
# 2. Identify the exact path (note the full directory name, e.g., pvc-abc123_ns_name)
# 3. Manually create a PV pointing to that directory
# 5. Patch the PVC to reference the recovery PV
# 7. After rebind confirmed, optionally change reclaimPolicy to Retain for safety

scenario_c_statefulset_pvcs.title: StatefulSet PVCs in Lost phase — rebind to existing data
scenario_c_statefulset_pvcs.note: StatefulSet PVC names follow pattern: {volumeClaimTemplate-name}-{pod-name}. Do NOT delete StatefulSet PVCs until data is secured — StatefulSet controller creates new empty PVCs on re-creation.
steps: # 1. Scale down the StatefulSet to prevent it from fighting recovery
# 2. Follow scenario_b steps for each PVC in Lost phase
# 3. After all PVCs rebound, scale up

prevention: Patch StorageClass reclaimPolicy to Retain for production PVCs (see hardening section)
Never run kubectl delete pv on a live volume without first confirming the PVC is safely deleted and data is backed up
Use Velero for PV backup before cluster maintenance

host_prep.description: Ubuntu 22.04 host preparation for /mnt/k3s-3-pv-data — mount verification, fstab UUID pinning, permissions
mount_verification: blkid /dev/sdX1  # replace sdX with actual device
# If disk is not formatted — format it (DESTRUCTIVE, skip if data exists)
fstab_uuid_pinning: # Get UUID (NEVER use /dev/sdX directly — device names shift after reboots)
permissions: # Set ownership for k3s local-path helper pods (run as root in container)
# Helper pods create subdirs inside; subdirs get 0777 via setup script
# Verify existing PVC subdirs are accessible
# If specific subdirs have wrong ownership (e.g., after manual migration):
systemd_mount_service: # Optional: add explicit systemd mount dependency for k3s
# This ensures k3s starts AFTER /mnt/k3s-3-pv-data is mounted

hardening.description: Post-repair hardening for stable production storage on /mnt/k3s-3-pv-data

stable_storageclass.description: Create a production StorageClass with Retain policy alongside the default local-path class

patch_existing_pvs_to_retain: # Change all existing PVs from Delete to Retain (protect data from accidental PVC deletion)
startup_health_check_script: # Run at boot or via cron: @reboot sleep 60 && /usr/local/bin/k3s-storage-healthcheck.sh
READY=$(kubectl get deploy -n kube-system local-path-provisioner -o jsonpath='{.status.readyReplicas}' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
LOST=$(kubectl get pvc -A -o json | jq '[.items[] | select(.status.phase=="Lost")] | length')
smoke_tests: # Smoke Test 1: Dynamic provisioning + pod mount
PV_PATH=$(kubectl get pvc smoke-test-pvc -n default -o jsonpath='{.spec.volumeName}' | xargs -I{} kubectl get pv {} -o jsonpath='{.spec.hostPath.path}')

storageclass_retain.yaml:
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: local-path-retain
  annotations:
    storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class: "false"
provisioner: rancher.io/local-path
reclaimPolicy: Retain
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
parameters:
  nodePath: /mnt/k3s-3-pv-data

patch_pv_retain.description: Patch a single PV to Retain

patch_pv_remove_claimref.description: Make a Released PV available for rebinding

recovery_pv_template.description: Manual PV template for orphaned on-disk data
recovery_pv_template.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata:
  name: recovery-pv-REPLACE
spec:
  capacity:
    storage: 10Gi
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain
  storageClassName: local-path
  hostPath:
    path: /mnt/k3s-3-pv-data/REPLACE_SUBDIR
    type: Directory
  nodeAffinity:
    required:
      nodeSelectorTerms:
        - matchExpressions:
            - key: kubernetes.io/hostname
              operator: In
              values:
                - REPLACE_NODE_NAME

anti_patterns: DELETING_PV_WITH_DELETE_POLICY — running kubectl delete pv on a Delete-policy PV while the directory exists on disk triggers provisioner cleanup (rm -rf); always patch to Retain first
EDITING_CONFIGMAP_ONLY — editing local-path-config ConfigMap without the skip-file pattern reverts on every k3s restart/upgrade
REINSTALLING_K3S — full k3s reinstall destroys etcd; PV objects are lost; data on disk survives only if you know the exact paths
WRONG_BUSYBOX_IMAGE — overriding helperPod.yaml with a busybox image not present in containerd causes all PVC provisions to silently hang
CHOWN_RECURSIVE_ON_LIVE_PVCS — running chown -R on /mnt/k3s-3-pv-data while pods are running can corrupt in-flight writes
DEVICE_NAME_IN_FSTAB — using /dev/sdX in fstab instead of UUID causes mount failure after kernel upgrades or SATA reordering
NO_NOFAIL_IN_FSTAB — missing nofail option causes boot hang if the SATA disk fails; always use 'defaults,nofail'

common_error_messages.failed to read config: ConfigMap local-path-config is missing or has malformed config.json
common_error_messages.permission denied mkdir: Host directory ownership or permissions wrong; fix with chown/chmod on /mnt/k3s-3-pv-data
common_error_messages.is forbidden: RBAC missing or broken; re-apply ClusterRole/ClusterRoleBinding
common_error_messages.ErrImagePull for helper-pod: rancher/mirrored-library-busybox image not in containerd; run: crictl pull rancher/mirrored-library-busybox:1.36.1
common_error_messages.PVC has non-bound phase Lost: PV object deleted or claimRef UID mismatch; follow pvc_lost_recovery procedure
common_error_messages.no such file or directory: Configured storage path does not exist on host or disk not mounted

success_criteria: kubectl get deploy -n kube-system local-path-provisioner -o jsonpath='{.status.readyReplicas}' == 1
kubectl get pvc -A -o json | jq '[.items[] | select(.status.phase=="Lost")] | length' == 0
Smoke test PVC binds and pod writes/reads successfully from /mnt/k3s-3-pv-data
After systemctl restart k3s, ConfigMap still points to /mnt/k3s-3-pv-data (skip-file pattern active)
All critical workload pods status Running with persistent volumes attached
truth_lens: k3s single-node local-path-provisioner recovery specialist: diagnoses CrashLoopBackOff via ordered root-cause checklist (ConfigMap validity, host path existence, RBAC integrity, file permissions, containerd images, k3s manifest overwrite, AppArmor), provides exact kubectl+host validation commands per failure mode, executes minimal-risk repair with explicit rollback at each step, recovers Lost-phase PVCs by patching claimRef or recreating PV objects against on-disk data, hardens storage with skip-file+custom-manifest pattern for upgrade persistence, Retain reclaimPolicy on production PVs, fstab UUID pinning with nofail, and a smoke test suite verifying end-to-end dynamic provisioning on /mnt/k3s-3-pv-data.
consult_when: local-path-provisioner is in CrashLoopBackOff or Error state on k3s
PVCs are in Lost or Pending phase on a k3s cluster
custom storage path /mnt/k3s-3-pv-data needs to be configured for local-path provisioner
k3s upgrade resets custom storage path (configmap revert issue)
Ubuntu 22.04 disk not mounting persistently for k3s PV storage
manual PV recovery after accidental kubectl delete pv
hardening k3s local storage with Retain policy and StatefulSet safety
smoke testing dynamic provisioning after storage reconfiguration
key_patterns: Pattern: map symptom → ordered checklist (ConfigMap → host path → RBAC → permissions → images → k3s manifest → AppArmor) before destructive PV/PVC deletes.
Pattern: Lost PVC → compare PV claimRef UID to PVC UID → patch or recreate PV against on-disk paths under nodePathMap; verify with jq smoke queries in success_criteria.
expertise: LOCAL_PATH_CONFIG — kube-system/local-path-config ConfigMap config.json nodePathMap and skip-file overlay for k3s upgrades
PVC_LOST_RECOVERY — claimRef UID mismatch, Retain reclaimPolicy, minimal recreation against existing hostDir data
HOST_DISK_U2204 — fstab UUID, nofail, mountpoint checks for /mnt/k3s-3-pv-data (or org-defined path)
